name: SJPW House Show — Owase City Gymnasium

matches.note: Thomas rolled up Kobayashi from behind for the pinfall after Douglas broke up the Crush Crew's own Assaiki attempt on him.
Jager applied the Strange Hold Beta as the time limit ran out; both men shook hands afterward.
Enforcer kicked out of a Russian Sickle, then scored the pinfall with a big chokeslam.

Booked as a follow-up to an angle from the same taping of The Zone!. Thunder scored the pinfall on Bakemono with the Widowmaker after KEOKI kicked out of Despair's Gunryo title-belt shot behind the referee's back.

notes: The opening show of the revival's own three-date house-show swing reported in one bulletin. The Gunryo Championship (the revival's own special title, per the fed's own F.A.Q.) is referred to by commentary as already held by Despair; no title-change document survives from before this run, so no reign is recorded here.

name: SJPW House Show — Shirihama Hall

matches.note: Tetsuhara scored the pinfall with a top-rope overhead belly-to-belly suplex into the Dragon Driver 1.
Liar pulled Jager's legs out from under him on the apron, and Matsuoko hit a Stun Gun on Enforcer, rolling him up for the pinfall.
Tasogare no Prince ended a losing streak, rolling out of a top-rope headbutt attempt and countering with the Destiny Driver for the pinfall.

The show's main event, given a standing ovation on introduction. Wrestling under his own name rather than his old masked gimmick, Matsumoto kicked out of Kawasaki's Hentai Holocaust before scoring the pinfall with his own Dragon Driver.

notes: The revival's own second stop on the same touring swing, two nights after Owase.

name: SJPW House Show — Chiimu Tora Dojo

matches.note: Larson caught a springboarding Ananda with a capture suplex, then scored the pinfall with a second powerbomb into the Jackhammer.
An upset: Asakura pulled Lanther off the top turnbuckle mid-headbutt and scored the pinfall with the Asakura Crusher. The two shook hands after.
A rematch of the Wakayama main event two nights earlier. Kawasaki evened the score, scoring the pinfall with a second Hentai Holocaust after Matsumoto kicked out of the first.

The show's main event. Despair struck KEOKI with the Gunryo title belt behind the referee's back, and Nakatoni scored the pinfall on a third Assaiki attempt. A post-match brawl followed: Kubota cleared the ring with a garbage-can lid, and Thunder drove Despair's head into his own title belt with the Widowmaker.

notes: The revival's own third and final stop on this touring swing, held at the Chiimu Tora Dojo training school itself before an audience of 300.

name: SJPW House Show — Okazaki City Gym

matches.note: A grudge rematch from an earlier Gunryo title free-for-all. Kubota low blowed Suzuki and worked him over, but Suzuki fired back with an Aloha Extreme for the pinfall.
Lanther and Jiraiya doubled up on Nakatoni late, and Jiraiya caught a diving Kobayashi with a springboard dropkick to let Lanther score the pinfall off a superplex.
Kwan, returning from a month-long injury with protege Ananda, was caught alone with Jager, who forced the submission with the Crossface Chicken Wing after Ananda couldn't break the hold in time.

A non-title main event: Bakemono refused to put the NCWF Cruiserweight Championship on the line, calling Azteca unworthy. Azteca upset him anyway, locking on the Azteca Speciale for the submission — his first big SJPW win.

notes: The revival's own next house show after the 19-24 April 2004 touring swing.

name: SJPW House Show — Okinawa Fight Club Kamikaze

matches.note: Ananda won by knockout after a spinning roundhouse kick left Davinsky unable to continue.
A Gunryo rules rematch from the Okazaki show: Kubota fireballed Suzuki and used a chain and a chair on him, but Suzuki fired back with two backdrop drivers and a Dragon Sleeper for the submission.
A stiff power match. Larson kicked out of Nishida's Raging Bull Bomber and scored the pinfall with the Jackhammer.
A well-received high-flying contest. TnP survived a springboard legdrop and a small package before hitting his own top-rope somersault legdrop, Nightfall, for the pinfall.
Botan Nakatoni ran in early to snap Thunder's neck on the top rope before being ordered from ringside. Thunder no-sold two Widowmakers and forced Kobayashi to submit to a standing Dragon Sleeper.

Main event, NCWF Cruiserweight Championship: Azteca, seconded by former long-time champion Masashi "Lightning" Lanther, nearly submitted Bakemono with a single leg crab, but the champion retained with a top-rope Bakemono Bomb. Despair (seconding Bakemono) attacked Azteca afterward; Lanther made the save and beat down Despair with his own Gunryo title belt; Bakemono then struck Lanther with the NCWF belt, and "Lone Wolf" Brody Thunder ran in, fighting off Bakemono before driving Despair's head into his own title belt with the Widowmaker.

notes: A sold-out, longer-than-usual card marking the revival's return to Okinawa.

name: SJPW House Show — Chiimu Tora Dojo (6/4/04)

matches.note: Kagawa filled in for his own trainer Tiger Kikuchi, who seconded him instead. After a hard-hitting back-and-forth, Kagawa caught a charging Larson with a spear for the pinfall.

Atashi took the veteran luchador the distance with a high-flying attack, but got cocky going for a dropkick; Azteca sidestepped, isolated the leg, and forced a submission to the figure-four leglock after a three-minute struggle.

Two visiting American cruiserweights, each already carrying a title from another promotion, traded near-falls including dueling top-rope Exploders before Darren scored the pinfall with a second All Star Frog Splash.

CEO Shinsaku Yamashita changed the scheduled main event, giving Tasogare no Prince the shot instead of Masashi Lanther. Kawasaki controlled most of the match, but after a long reversal sequence off a sunset flip, Tasogare no Prince came away with the pinfall in an upset.

notes: The Dojo's own head trainer Tiger Kikuchi introduced four recent graduates before the card (Dragon Mask, Toramusha, MAMMOTH Kagawa, and the tag team the Nagasaki Bulldogs); CEO Yamashita also announced a barbed-wire steel cage crossover match against an outside promotion, not contested under SJPW's own banner.

name: SJPW House Show — Tokyo Club Atom (6/6/04)

matches.note: The debuting Dojo graduates Dragon Mask & Toramusha made a good showing, but their inexperience told in the end: Tetsuhara made Dragon Mask submit to a triangle choke at 7:42.

Azteca's own quest for a shot at Despair's Gunryo Championship continued against a former champion of an unrelated Japanese promotion. Hori scored several near-falls, but Azteca's experience won out with the Aztec Suplex at 12:22.

The debuting Nagasaki Bulldogs upset the veteran Crush Crew at 9:03, Dynamite Boy pinning Nakatoni with the team's own double-team finisher after Nakatoni had promised to use a win here to petition for a shot at an outside promotion's own tag team.
A stiff battle of Chiimu Tora Dojo powerhouses. Nishida sidestepped Kagawa's own MAMMOTH Charge spear, sending him into the corner, and scored the pinfall with an Exploder at 5:15.

A high-spot main event; Lanther pinned Bakemono with the Lanther Bomb at 14:27 after Jiraiya dropkicked Despair to the floor. Lanther told Bakemono afterward that he would reclaim the NCWF Cruiserweight Championship from him at Zenmen Sensou.

notes: A results bulletin for a 230-fan sellout crowd; no commentary text accompanies this document.

name: SJPW House Show — Battle Sphere Tokyo (6/8/04)

matches.note: Dragon Mask's singles debut was closely fought against the slightly more experienced Jet Jaguar III, who won with a Fisherman's Falcon Arrow at 8:19; both men shook hands afterward.

The Maulers, billed here by their own full names, stopped the Nagasaki Bulldogs from repeating their upset of two nights earlier, hitting the Mauler Plex (a superplex onto the opponent) on Shimura at 10:32.
Tetsuo Matsumoto evened his own series with Asakura, dumping him with a half-nelson suplex for the pinfall at 14:07 after Asakura appeared close to a win.

The two visiting Americans, rivals four days earlier, showed strong chemistry as a team; Tsunami pinned Toramusha with a Tsunami Driver #2 at 7:28 while Darren held off Azteca from breaking up the count.

Jager worked the arm throughout, but Kawasaki shoved off an armbreaker attempt and scored the pinfall with the Ecchi Driver at 12:45. After the match a man came out of the stands and led Jager away without a struggle; Kawasaki left with Mysterious Warrior.

notes: A results bulletin for a 300-fan sellout crowd; no commentary text accompanies this document.

name: SJPW House Show — Katsushika Ward Center Bunka Hall

matches.note: Ananda pinned the debuting Baranov, Gregor Davinsky's nephew, after the Ananda Special.
"Firefly" Horo Atashi defeated the veteran Yatoro Hori with a superkick in a short, fast-paced bout; both men shook hands after.
Azteca, continuing his quest to face Despair, teamed with the rookie Kagawa to make Nakatoni submit to a hanging armbar; Nakatoni's arm was hurt badly enough that he needed hospital treatment.
Despair's first official Gunryo Championship defense: a weapons-heavy brawl (Kubota nailed him with a flaming chair) that Despair won with a belly-to-belly moonsault through a table.
Tommy Fury, debuting as a substitute for Joey Darren (who had to fly home to defend his ICW Network title), pinned Takahiro KEOKI with the Legend Killer.

notes: 350 fans, a sellout. Sergei Baranov (Gregor Davinsky's nephew) and "Living Legend" Tommy Fury both debuted on this card.

name: SJPW House Show — Kitazawa Town Hall

matches.note: "Firefly" Horo Atashi superkicked a chair out of the masked El Gato Loco's hands and into his own face, stunning him long enough to score the pinfall.
Tsunami pinned Darren with the Tsunami Driver #1, adding intensity to their own building Zenmen Sensou rivalry.
Fury's first SJPW singles match: he outwrestled Douglas and pinned him with a bridging Dragon Suplex.

Toroyama, now on Team Tiger's most wanted list, joined the monster Hayatashi to face his own former partner and trainer Nishida and the rookie Kagawa; Toroyama pinned Nishida with a Jackknife Powerbomb. Kagawa afterward vowed on the microphone to beat Toroyama at Zenmen Sensou and "drive him out of Super Japan for good."

Despair's second Gunryo Championship defense: he worked over the former SMASH JHW champion Yatoro Hori's arm and shoulder with a singapore cane before forcing the tap-out with the Human Torment. Afterward Despair told the crowd he would retain the title against Takahiro KEOKI at Zenmen Sensou, calling himself the true "Ugly American."

notes: 250 fans, a sellout. El Gato Loco, Junya Toroyama (a returning former SJPW trainee) and "The Wolverine" Masuhiro Hayatashi all debuted on this card.

name: SJPW House Show — Tokyo FM Hall

matches.note: The Nagasaki Bulldogs, a new tandem of former SMASH Wrestling stars, defeated two Gunryo-division veterans; Dynamite Boy scored the pin with a top-rope headbutt on Hori. Afterward the Bulldogs promised the crowd they would beat the Visual Spirits in their own special tag challenge.
A fast-paced match between Jet Jaguar III and the rookie Toramusha, decided by the Jaguar Special; the two shook hands both before and after.
The rookie Dragon Mask forced Kobayashi to tap out to his own Dragon Sleeper; Kobayashi swore afterward to teach the rookie a lesson.
Azteca, continuing his road to Despair, caught Kwan's leg with a dragonscrew and made him submit to the Azteca Speciale.

Darren and Fury outlasted Tsunami and the SMLL trios champion El Gato Loco; Darren pinned Tsunami, the IICW Cruiserweight champion, with the Falling Star DDT, then mimed wearing the title belt, drawing Tsunami's anger.

notes: 275 fans. Held the same night as SJPW CEO Shinsaku Yamashita's press conference announcing the Zenmen Sensou card, at the same venue.

name: SJPW House Show — Chiba Bridge Arena Sub Arena

matches.note: Baranov avenged his own debut-night loss to Ananda, knocking him out with an Exploder '98.
Toramusha's first singles win, over the Crush Crew's Nakatoni, with a bridging Tiger Suplex '85.
The Maulers took the fight to Suzuki and the debuting monster Hayatashi early, but Suzuki forced Douglas to tap to his own version of the Sharpshooter.
Tetsuhara debuted his half-nelson, half Chicken Wing Dragon Fury Suplex to put away the debuting masked luchador.

Team Tiger avenged a recent six-man loss to Toroyama: after Dragon Mask & KEOKI double-teamed him, Kagawa speared Toroyama for the pin. Kagawa again vowed on the microphone to beat Toroyama at Zenmen Sensou with the MAMMOTH Charge.

notes: 400 fans, a sellout. "Dragon Fury" Minobu Tetsuhara's opponent, a masked luchador newcomer billed as Mascara Negra, debuted on this card.

name: SJPW House Show — Chiba Central Plaza

matches.note: Ananda gained revenge for his 18 June knockout loss, putting Baranov away with the springboard spinning roundhouse Ananda Special.
The young duo of Dragon Mask & Toramusha upset the more experienced pairing, Dragon Mask pinning Jaguar III with the Dragon Crush Drop.
Horo Atashi's latest win, over El Gato Loco, with a Thunder Fire Driver.
Lanther scored three near-falls on Nakatoni with the Lanther Bomb, each broken up by Kobayashi, who then pinned Jiraiya himself with a pumphandle Uranage.

A special non-title four-corners main event: after Despair moonsaulted KEOKI, Tsunami hit Despair with a Tsunami Driver #3, Darren caught Tsunami with the Falling Star, and KEOKI dropkicked Darren to the floor before finishing Despair with a cross-arm fisherman's buster. KEOKI told the crowd afterward that at Zenmen Sensou he would beat Despair "at his own game."

notes: 421 fans.

name: SJPW House Show — Iwase Townsman Gymnasium

matches.note: The debuting El Muerte Rojo joined El Gato Loco, billed together as the SMLL trios champions, to defeat the new team of Jaguar III & Toramusha.
Two big men battled to a 15-minute time-limit draw; Toroyama had the edge late with a series of Lariats when time ran out.
The unlikely duo of Fury & Atashi upset Team Tiger's Dragon Mask & Kagawa; Atashi nailed a dazed Dragon Mask with a top-rope flying lariat for the pin.
A fast, short match, decided by a top-rope Sunset Flip after Tasogare no Prince stunned Negra with an enzugiri.

Booked as a bizarre pairing-off of Zenmen Sensou's own two main-event rivalries: Asakura & Kawasaki worked better as a team than the bickering Despair & KEOKI, and Kawasaki pinned KEOKI with the Hentai Holocaust while Asakura held off Despair. Afterward Despair and KEOKI brawled; KEOKI dropkicked a chair into Despair's face and sent him over the railing before Dragon Mask & Kagawa pulled KEOKI away, and Despair warned the crowd he had something planned for KEOKI at Zenmen Sensou beyond a simple win.

notes: 371 fans. El Muerte Rojo debuted on this card, teaming with fellow SMLL wrestler El Gato Loco.

name: SJPW House Show — Chiimu Tora Dojo (6/24/04)

matches.note: Tetsuhara outwrestled Loco's dirty tactics and closed it out with a bridging German Suplex.

The Nagasaki Bulldogs avenged their own first loss, taking down the Maulers; Shimura pinned Douglas with a tilt-o'-whirl driver. Dynamite Boy promised afterward that the Bulldogs would show the Visual Spirits who the best tag team really was.
Fury's latest singles win since signing with Super Japan, over Team Tiger's Jun Kikuchi, by spinebuster.
Kagawa & Nishida showed the better teamwork over a hesitant, mistrustful Toroyama & Suzuki, finishing with a double chokeslam on Toroyama. Suzuki and Toroyama then brawled, emptying the locker room.

The visiting SMLL luchadors, more accustomed to trios matches, kept the Disciples of Despair off balance; El Muerte Rojo won it with a top-rope Muerte Driver #1 on Bakemono. Despair then attacked Azteca & Negra outside the ring with his own Gunryo title belt, only for Muerte Rojo to hit him with a corkscrew plancha; as the Disciples of Despair ganged up on Rojo, Takahiro KEOKI ran in with Despair's own barbed-wire steel chair, cracking it over the Disciples and busting Despair open. Despair swore afterward that KEOKI's suffering at Zenmen Sensou would not be forgotten.

notes: 300 fans, a sellout — the last house show before the revival's own first supershow, Zenmen Sensou. Jun Kikuchi debuted on this card.

name: Zenmen Sensou Press Conference
no_appearances_reason: A press-conference broadcast announcing an upcoming supershow's card and a talent-exchange arrangement with two outside promotions -- not a wrestling card in its own right.
notes: CEO Shinsaku Yamashita announced the full nine-match Zenmen Sensou card at the 5,500-seat Budokan Hall, plus a talent exchange with Super Mexico Lucha Libre (SMLL) and a showcase match with the American Pro Wrestling Glory promotion. The supershow itself (26 June 2004) was posted to the newsgroup only as a link to an off-site results page, which does not survive in the held record.

name: SJPW House Show — Kanagawa Jd' Dojo (6/28/04)

matches.note: El Gato Loco scored his first win over Mascara Negra with a twisting moonsault (10:03) after the Tornillo Gato.

The Crush Crew defeated the Nagasaki Bulldogs (10:45) after the Assaiki (a 3D over the top rope) on Shimura, following a pre-match microphone exchange over the Bulldogs' loss to the Visual Spirits at Zenmen Sensou.
"Firefly" Horo Atashi defeated "Dragon Fury" Minobu Tetsuhara (16:00) after a top rope sunset flip.
Kenichi Kubota & Yatoro Hori defeated Despair & Super Bakemono (13:26) after the Kurassha Driver on Despair.

Dragon Mask, Jet Jaguar III & Toramusha defeated Gregor Davinsky, Wolf Jager & Sergei Baranov (22:17) after a Jaguar Special on Jager, in a six-man contrast of the masked men's aerial style against the EuroPack's mat-based approach.

notes: A results bulletin; no separate commentary text beyond the recap prose accompanies this document.

name: SJPW House Show — Yokosuka Rinkai Park (6/30/04)

matches.note: "Firefly" Horo Atashi defeated the veteran Se-hong Kwan (8:37) after a Frog Splash.
The Maulers defeated Team Raiden (12:55) after a spiked powerbomb on Lanther.
"Dragon Fury" Minobu Tetsuhara and Junya Toroyama fought to a 20:00 draw, not part of Tiger Kikuchi's Five Fight Challenge series; Toroyama scored seven near falls before time expired.

Gregor Davinsky, Wolf Jager & Sergei Baranov defeated Dragon Mask, Jet Jaguar III & Toramusha (17:29) after Jager made Jaguar III submit to the Strangle Hold Beta, a rematch grudge from two days earlier.
Tasogare no Prince & Tsunami defeated Kentaro Kawasaki & Tommy Fury (18:04) after TnP pinned Kawasaki following a Destiny Driver, TnP's second win over Kawasaki.

notes: A results bulletin; no separate commentary text beyond the recap prose accompanies this document.

name: SJPW House Show — SAPPORO BREWERIES Factory Hall (7/5/04)

matches.note: Junior Struggle! Block A: Toramusha upset Jet Jaguar III (9:45) with the Tiger Suplex '85, both men shaking hands before and after.
Junior Struggle! Block B: "Kyoto Tiger" Takayoshi Asakura defeated Yatoro Hori (8:04) with the Firebird Splash, rebounding from his own Zenmen Sensou loss to Kawasaki.

Noboru "Raging Bull" Nishida & MAMMOTH Kagawa, a new Team Tiger pairing, defeated the Crush Crew (13:19) after a double Nodowa Otashi on Kobayashi; Nishida told the crowd afterward the pair would repeat the win against the Crush Crew at Pro Wrestling Glory's American debut show.
Junior Struggle! Block A: "Firefly" Horo Atashi defeated the debuting Fanta Boy (10:27) with a moonsault, Atashi's first tournament win.

Junior Struggle! Block B: Super Bakemono, reeling from his own Zenmen Sensou loss to Lanther, upset Tsunami, reeling from his own loss of the IICW title to Joey Darren, (20:09) after countering a Tsunami Driver attempt with a mule kick, a Michinoku Driver, and finally the Bakemono Bomb.

notes: A results bulletin; no separate commentary text beyond the recap prose accompanies this document.

name: SJPW House Show — Esashi Town Center Gymnasium (7/7/04)

matches.note: Junior Struggle! Block A: the new IICW cruiserweight champion Joey Darren defeated Toramusha (9:17) after countering a top-rope powerbomb attempt with a hurricanrana.
Junior Struggle! Block B: Wolf Jager made Yatoro Hori (0-2) submit to the Strangle Hold Beta (10:09) after ducking a second superkick attempt and working the arm.
"Dragon Fury" Minobu Tetsuhara & El Santa Azteca defeated two of SMLL's more bizarre competitors (12:22) after Tetsuhara, frustrated by Fanta Boy's antics, hit a wrist-clutch Exploder.
Junior Struggle! Block A: the debuting Mr. Smiley Mask made Jet Jaguar III go 0-2 (12:48) after his high-angle shooting star press he calls "Shit Happens"; both men shook hands afterward.
Junior Struggle! Block B: the rookie Takahiro KEOKI upset the veteran Tsunami (15:00) after a High Impact Driver, following a Tsunami Driver #1 near-fall; both shook hands afterward.

notes: A results bulletin; no separate commentary text beyond the recap prose accompanies this document.

name: SJPW House Show — Zepp Sapporo (7/9/04)

matches.note: Junior Struggle! Block A: Fanta Boy scored his first tournament win over Toramusha (8:37) after a top rope Blue Thunder Driver, billed in the results line as "the Apple Sauce."

Van Wild & Scott Starring, entered in the upcoming GPH Tag League, defeated El Gato Loco & Mascara Negra (12:02) following a combination Side Slam/Top Rope Legdrop on Negra in their SJPW debut, drawing a warm streamer welcome from the crowd.

Five Fight Challenge, Match Two: Junya Toroyama defeated Eiji Kid Shimura (7:28) after a Last Ride-style powerbomb, following an STO and a Nodowa Otashi; Tiger Kikuchi told Toroyama afterward his next opponent would be his own former tag partner, Noboru "Raging Bull" Nishida.

The Red Army made their SJPW debut, defeating Se-hong Kwan & El Muerte Rojo (9:50) after a double Stun Gun on Kwan onto the top rope, following a near-fall for Muerte Rojo's own Muerte Rojo Driver #1 on Tarasov.
Junior Struggle! Block B: Wolf Jager defeated the still-winless Tsunami (11:59) after an Exploder to the injured shoulder; both shook hands afterward.

"GAIJIN Extreme" Jun Suzuki & "The Wolverine" Masuhiro Hayatashi defeated "Lone Wolf" Brody Thunder & "Jackhammer" Vince Larson (13:04) after a ref-bump spot in which Suzuki blasted Thunder with his chair, then hit the Widowmaker onto it while Hayatashi dragged the referee over; a post-match brawl saw the locker room empty to separate Thunder and Suzuki, after which Thunder took the microphone to vow he was not retiring.

notes: A results bulletin; no separate commentary text beyond the recap prose accompanies this document.

name: SJPW House Show — Tokyo Club ATOM (7/11/04)

matches.note: GPH Tag League: "Hard" Knox Roberts & "Terrible" Tommy Bedford, in their SJPW debut, defeated the Nagasaki Bulldogs (12:34) after Roberts distracted the referee to allow a low blow, then Bedford's Cradle Piledriver ("Quittin' Time") on Dynamite Boy.
Junior Struggle! Block A: "Firefly" Horo Atashi defeated Toramusha (9:09) via submission to a Fujiwara armbar.

GPH Tag League: the Visual Spirits, rebounding from a loss of the Sapporo City Tag Titles elsewhere, defeated The Maulers (14:54) after KANJI caught Douglas with the Violence Flash while Hiroto held off Thomas; the crowd applauded the Spirits, unaccustomed support that left both men visibly perplexed.
Junior Struggle! Block B: Tsunami scored his first tournament win over the still-winless Yatoro Hori (8:01) after the Tsunami Driver #2.

A ten-man scramble-rules tag match: Andresku pinned Bakemono (22:15) with a Russian Sickle after Bakemono had barely survived Andresku's own Red Square, and after Jet Jaguar III's missile dropkick knocked Despair off the apron as he tried to make the save; Despair needed help to the back, raising doubt over his readiness to defend the Gunryo title against Se-hong Kwan two days later.

notes: A results bulletin; no separate commentary text beyond the recap prose accompanies this document.

name: SJPW House Show — Kitazawa Town Hall (7/14/04)

matches.note: El Gato Loco won his first SJPW singles victory over fellow luchador Fanta Boy (7:57) by submission to the Medio Cangrejo.

GPH Tag League: Van Wild & Scott Starring defeated The Maulers (14:41) with the Crossfire (a Van Wild superplex/Starring moonsault combination) on Thomas; both teams shook hands and the fans threw streamers for both.
"Dragon Fury" Minobu Tetsuhara defeated Junya Toroyama (13:28) with a top rope wrist-clutch Exploder.

A scramble-rules trios match: Team Raiden & Azteca defeated Mascara Negra, Dragon Mask & "Kyoto Tiger" Takayoshi Asakura (12:09) after Lanther made Dragon Mask submit to an Octopus hold, despite a near-fall for Asakura's own Skytwister moonsault.
Gunryo Championship: Despair and Se-hong Kwan wrestled to a double knockout (18:54) after both men traded chairshots; Despair retained the title, and both men were stretchered out.

notes: A results bulletin; the show's subject line reads "Kite Town Hall," but the bulletin's own dateline and body both name the venue Kitazawa Town Hall (already established as a served venue on 14 June 2004), and this page follows the body text.

name: SJPW House Show — Tokyo Oi Store (7/19/04)

matches.note: GPH Tag League: the Red Army scored their first tag win, defeating the Crush Crew (11:04) with a Doomsday Device clothesline after a stiff, elbow-heavy contest.
El Muerte Rojo defeated Dragon Mask (9:47) following a hanging Full Nelson dropped into a sitout facebuster (billed as a Cristo del Muerte) in a technical showcase.

GPH Tag League: the Visual Spirits, in a rematch of their Zenmen Sensou meeting, defeated the Nagasaki Bulldogs (12:50) with a Back Drop Suplex/Guillotine Legdrop double team, KANJI's top-rope legdrop finishing Dynamite Boy.
"GAIJIN Extreme" Jun Suzuki defeated Gregor Davinsky (8:11) with a running Lariat, following a high-impact Chokeslam, in front of a crowd firmly behind Davinsky.

Grand Prix Heritage Championship: Kentaro Kawasaki's first title defense against Noboru "Raging Bull" Nishida ended in a thirty-minute time-limit draw; Nishida scored two near-falls (a powerbomb, a superplex counter) and Kawasaki hit the Hentai Holocaust for a near-fall of his own broken up by a foot on the ropes. Kawasaki retained the title and left with the belt, ignoring Nishida's challenge to continue.

notes: Posted to the newsgroup twice on the same day under identical text (Message-IDs c363afc.0407201000.57dc3651@posting.google.com and c363afc.0407201029.4e0b0cfc@posting.google.com); this page serves the earlier-timestamped post and records the duplicate as collected, not separately served.

name: SJPW House Show — Chiimu Tora Dojo (8/11/04)

matches.note: Takahiro KEOKI defeated Dynamite Boy (8:41) with a series of Fisherman's suplexes topped off by the Uzumaki Toubida, opening a Team Tiger fan-club show at Tiger Kikuchi's own dojo.
Jet Jaguar III & Toramusha, teaming for the first time, defeated Dragon Mask & Jiraiya (10:39) after Toramusha stunned Dragon Mask with a release Tiger Suplex before both men hit Total Elimination.
"Dragon Fury" Minobu Tetsuhara defeated Eiji Kid Shimura (9:22) after dumping him with an Exploder '98, then making him submit to the Dragon Sleeper.

A three-way match: Noboru "Raging Bull" Nishida defeated his own tag partner MAMMOTH Kagawa and Jun Kikuchi (14:45) with the Raging Bull Bomber on Kikuchi, after Kikuchi had taken Kagawa out with a Dangerous Backdrop Driver.

NCWF Cruiserweight title: champion Masashi "Lightning" Lanther and challenger Shoji Suzuki, taking time off from his commitments in Visual Spirit Pro, wrestled to a twenty-minute time-limit draw after a back-and-forth stiff-strike exchange; Lanther retained. Both men signed autographs with fans for ninety minutes afterward, and fans expressed hope Suzuki would get a rematch with Tora Waziname in VSP.

notes: A results bulletin; no separate commentary text beyond the recap prose accompanies this document.

name: SJPW House Show — Fukaya City Shiba Central Park (8/16/04)

matches.note: Scott Starring defeated El Gato Loco (5:20) with The Rookie Mistake (a shooting star press) after countering a chair shot attempt with a superkick and an X-factor onto the chair, opening SJPW's three-show Saitama run.

MAMMOTH Kagawa & Noboru "Raging Bull" Nishida defeated "The Wolverine" Masuhiro Hayatashi & Kenichi Kubota (10:50) with the MAMMOTH Charge! on Hayatashi, after Nishida rallied from a near-fall Chokeslam from Hell.
Junya Toroyama scored an upset win over "Living Legend" Tommy Fury (13:08) with a high angle powerbomb, after fighting back from a figure-four leglock to a corner avalanche and bulldog.

Team Raiden defeated Despair & Super Bakemono (17:24) after a koppo kick sent Despair from the apron to the floor and Lanther, especially rough with his own former student, hit the Lanther Bomb on Bakemono, who had hesitated to attack his own mentor.

IICW Cruiserweight title: champion "All-Star" Joey Darren defeated challenger Fanta Boy (14:00) with the All-Star Frog Splash, after countering Fanta Boy's ring antics with a Manhattan Drop and a tornado DDT.

notes: Crowd was noted extremely pleased with the card, and discussed Bakemono's reluctance to attack his own former mentor Lanther, wondering whether his new partnership with Junya Toroyama had softened his attitude toward Team Tiger.

name: SJPW House Show — Kamisato Townsman Gymnasium (8/18/04)

matches.note: Scott Starring defeated Dragon Mask (11:55) with a Shining Wizard kneestrike, after kicking out of a Dragon Suplex and rolling out of a sunset flip.
The Red Army defeated SMASH Attack (as Hori & Kubota bill themselves) (10:12) after Tarasov made Hori submit to the Iron Curtain crossface, following Andresku's own power domination of Hori.
"Dragon Fury" Minobu Tetsuhara outwrestled the submission specialist Botan Nakatoni (12:00) with the Dragon Driver 1.

A six-man scramble: GPH Champion Kentaro Kawasaki teamed with the Visual Spirits to defeat Tasogare no Prince, Takahiro KEOKI & "Firefly" Horo Atashi (17:54) after KANJI pinned TnP with the Violence Flash, following a Kawasaki/TnP exchange that saw both men trade near-falls.

IICW Cruiserweight title: champion Joey Darren made a second Saitama defense against Jiraiya (10:23), pinning him with a new flipping piledriver after Jiraiya nearly won with a Northern Lights Suplex.

notes: Fans discussed after the show when Tasogare no Prince would get his own shot at Kawasaki's title, following the trios main event.

name: SJPW House Show — Kawamoto Town Training Center (8/20/04, daytime)

matches.note: Scott Starring defeated Dynamite Boy (12:45) with a top rope Missile Dropkick, after avoiding a top rope headbutt, in a preview of the two teams' GPH Tag League match on the night's second show.
Team Raiden defeated two of the SMLL International Trios champions, El Gato Negro & El Muerte Rojo, (13:21) with their own Lightning Strike version of Total Elimination on El Gato Negro.
Van Wild defeated the other half of the Nagasaki Bulldogs, Eiji Kid Shimura, (10:15) with a brainbuster.

Despair & Super Bakemono, a more engaged Bakemono this time, defeated Jet Jaguar III & Toramusha (14:24) after Toramusha's release Tiger Suplex was answered by Koppo kicks, an enzugiri, and the Bakemono Driver.
"Living Legend" Tommy Fury evened his own series with Junya Toroyama (16:39) with a top rope overhead belly-to-belly suplex, after working Toroyama's back with backbreakers and a boston crab.

notes: A daytime event closing SJPW's week-long Saitama run; the bulletin notes a same-day evening card at the Gyoda Citizen Gymnasium and that this document classes El Gato Negro as distinct from El Gato Loco, who wrestles the same week under his own name elsewhere on the tour; both spellings are as written.

name: SJPW House Show — Gyoda Citizen Gymnasium (8/20/04, evening)

matches.note: GPH Tag League: the Visual Spirits, fan favorites despite themselves, defeated the Crush Crew (12:35) after Hiroto's series of Yakuza kicks left Hiroto pinning Nakatoni following a second Yakuza kick.
Mr. Smiley Mask, arriving in the Smileymobile, defeated Yatoro Hori (8:50) with Sh*t Happens, after a dragonscrew legwhip and a single-leg crab.
GPH Tag League: Van Wild & Scott Starring defeated the Nagasaki Bulldogs (11:48) when Van Wild superplexed his own partner Starring onto Dynamite Boy for the pinfall.

Jet Jaguar III defeated Super Bakemono (17:19) with a Spiral Bomb, the finisher of the man who trained J3, Shoji Suzuki; Bakemono offered his hand after the match, and J3 accepted it to a torrent of streamers.
GPH Tag League: "Hard" Knox Roberts & "Terrible" Tommy Bedford defeated The Maulers (12:28) after Roberts hit a series of punches and a DDT on Thomas.

IICW Cruiserweight title: champion Joey Darren defended for a third time in the week against Mascara Negra (18:18), retaining with the All-Star Driver after Negra had earlier kicked out of the All-Star Frog Splash.

notes: Closed out a week-long Saitama tour; the crowd discussed Darren's three title defenses in one week and Bakemono's continued rapport with Toroyama's side of the SJPW roster.

name: SJPW House Show — Katsushika Ward Center Bunka Hall (8/23/04)

matches.note: Scott Starring defeated Jiraiya (12:25) with a top rope hurricanrana, returning SJPW to Tokyo.
Junior Struggle! Block B: Super Bakemono kept Yatoro Hori (of SMASH Attack) winless in the tournament (9:09) with a springboard DDT.
Tsunami, beginning a comeback for the IICW title, defeated El Gato Loco (13:40) with the Tsunami Driver #3.
Junior Struggle! Block A: "Firefly" Horo Atashi defeated Jet Jaguar III (16:05) with a yakuza kick, after J3's own Jaguar Special was kicked out of.

A four-team scramble tag: the EuroPack's Gregor Davinsky & his nephew Sergei Baranov won a preview of the upcoming Gunryo tag gauntlet (22:17), Baranov pinning Sangre Guerrero of the Blood Merchants with a Tiger Suplex '95 after Guerrero missed a frog splash.

notes: A great show that returned SJPW to its home turf of Tokyo, per the bulletin's own closing line.

name: SJPW House Show — Tokyo Marine (8/25/04)

matches.note: Tsunami continued his comeback, defeating Fanta Boy (8:59) with a brainbuster.
The Maulers defeated Noboru "Raging Bull" Nishida & MAMMOTH Kagawa (12:32) after Thomas worked Kagawa's leg down to an anklelock submission.

Super Bakemono defeated Scott Starring (13:04) with an inverted Tornado DDT from the top rope, after both men traded a high-flying sequence including a Starring springboard moonsault and a Bakemono guillotine legdrop.
The IICW & NCWF champions, Joey Darren & Masashi Lanther, defeated "Firefly" Horo Atashi & Mr. Smiley Mask (12:54) after Lanther superkicked Smiley while Darren hit the All-Star Driver on Atashi.

The Rumble Pro champion Van Wild defeated Junya Toroyama (15:46) with a Dangerous Backdrop Driver, in a stiff main event that ended with a standing ovation and both men's partners joining them in a show of mutual respect; Despair was seen scowling from the entranceway.

notes: The card's main event closed with both teams (Toroyama/Bakemono and Van Wild/Starring, set to face off days later in the GPH Tag League) standing together in the ring; fans speculated afterward about Bakemono's changing allegiances and Despair's visible disapproval.

name: SJPW House Show — Tokyo Jiyugaoka Station Square Shoji Town SAKURA BANK Parking Lot (8/29/04)
venue: Tokyo Jiyugaoka Station Square Shoji Town SAKURA BANK Parking Lot

matches.note: Tsunami defeated Mascara Negra (10:15) with a brainbuster, continuing his comeback trail toward the IICW title.

GPH Tag League: Noboru "Raging Bull" Nishida & MAMMOTH Kagawa defeated Junya Toroyama & Super Bakemono (11:27) after Kagawa's MAMMOTH Charge! on Bakemono, who showed fighting spirit despite being the smallest man in the ring.

"Black Wasp" Akira Saito made his SJPW debut, defeating Fanta Boy (9:22) with his "Will O' Wasp" (a Diamond Dust variant); the bulletin notes this Akira Saito is not to be confused with the Akira Saito of the NorthPac Coalition.
SMASH Attack (Kenichi Kubota & Yatoro Hori) scored their first win as a team, defeating the EuroPack (12:50) after Kubota's Kurashaa Driver on Baranov, previewing the upcoming Gunryo tag gauntlet.

"GAIJIN Extreme" Jun Suzuki, originally scheduled to face Brody Thunder before Thunder's J*STAR signing, instead defeated a volunteering Jun Kikuchi (11:02) with the Aloha Extreme, after Kikuchi nearly won with Thunder's own Widowmaker; Suzuki tried to continue the attack afterward but was driven off by Nishida & Kagawa.

The two men set to determine the first Sedei-X champion, Horo Atashi & Joey Darren, defeated Takahiro KEOKI & Team Raiden's Masashi Lanther (13:35) after Darren's All-Star Driver on KEOKI set up Atashi's superkick for the pin, while Darren hit a corkscrew plancha on Lanther.

Main event, SMLL International Trios title defense: the Blood Merchants (El Gato Loco, El Muerte Rojo & Sangre Guerrero) retained against the Disciples of Despair (15:06), El Gato Loco pinning Despair with the Tornillo Gato after Guerrero's Tombstone Piledriver and Red Mist; Despair swore revenge on Muerte Rojo & Guerrero for J*STAR after the Blood Merchants dropkicked his own chair into his face.

notes: A big weekend show promoting the coming J*STAR festival in America; the promotion booked extra matches for the sellout crowd.

name: SJPW House Show — Meguro AJW Garage (8/30/04)

matches.note: The Crush Crew, rebounding from their trios loss the day before, defeated Se-hong Kwan & Pramoj Ananda (11:08) after a running Lariat by Kobayashi knocked Kwan out.
Tsunami's comeback continued, defeating the SMASH Attack member Yatoro Hori (9:49) with a top rope DDT.
The Maulers had a harder time than expected with Kenichi Kubota & El Gato Loco, finally winning (14:22) with a Powerbomb/neckbreaker combination on Gato Loco after both challengers scored near-falls.
A submission match: Wolf Jager defeated "Living Legend" Tommy Fury (19:37) with the Strangle Hold Gamma, after a double underhook shoulderbreaker.

notes: A short four-match show at the AJW Garage the day after the big Jiyugaoka weekend card.

name: SJPW House Show — Shinjuku ACB Hall (9/1/04)

matches.note: Mr. Smiley Mask defeated Mascara Negra (9:29) with Sh*t Happens, after his own match was briefly interrupted breaking up a scuffle in the crowd between rival fans.
Tsunami defeated Sangre Guerrero (10:51) with a Fisherman's Falcon Arrow, avoiding the Sangre Mist Attack.

In the second Blood Merchants/DoD confrontation, Despair defeated El Gato Loco (11:04) with a top rope Inverted DDT; Sangre Guerrero made the save afterward, blinding Despair with the Sangre Mist Attack.

Main event: Team Raiden & Takahiro KEOKI defeated Joey Darren, "Firefly" Horo Atashi & "Kyoto Tiger" Takayoshi Asakura (15:23) after KEOKI caught Atashi in a sleeper turned into the High Impact Driver.

notes: Billed as a small show ahead of a bigger Friday card at the Shinjuku Island Hall before the J*STAR festival in America.
